hooks.text: A tiny dwarf galaxy bullied a spiral twice our size.
A runaway spiral arm is stretching this giant galaxy apart.
What pulled an entire spiral galaxy completely out of shape?

title: The Dwarf Galaxy That Warped a Giant
description: A dwarf galaxy gravitationally pulled spiral galaxy NGC 772 out of shape, creating a runaway arm that erupted with supernovae.

beats.text: A tiny dwarf galaxy bullied a spiral twice our size.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope view of asymmetric spiral galaxy NGC 772, 2019

beats.text: Our Milky Way spans a balanced pinwheel of sweeping, orderly spiral arms.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of the Milky Way galaxy showing its symmetric spiral arms, 2008

beats.text: Look across the constellation Aries, and unbarred spiral galaxy NGC 772 is significantly larger than our home galaxy.
beats.visual: Aries constellation star chart showing the celestial location of NGC 772, 2010

beats.text: Yet its symmetry is shattered. NGC 772 is radically lopsided, dominated by one colossal runaway arm packed with dust lanes.
beats.visual: Wide astrophotograph of NGC 772 highlighting its single dominant spiral arm, 2021

beats.text: The cosmic culprit is NGC 770, a nearby dwarf elliptical galaxy.
beats.visual: Telescope image of dwarf elliptical galaxy NGC 770 near NGC 772, 2019

beats.text: Its relentless gravitational tides dragged and compressed the giant's disk, triggering furious stellar nurseries.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope close-up of dark dust lanes in NGC 772, 2019

beats.text: Star birth ran so violently that two separate Type II supernovae detonated in NGC 772 just seven weeks apart in 2003.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a core-collapse Type II supernova explosion in space, 2013

beats.text: Immense size could not protect this warped giant from an underdog.
beats.visual: Deep space photograph of interacting galaxy pair Arp 78 in Aries, 2021

better_than_last: Applies lessons from ep086 and ep114 by structuring comparisons as an escalating scale ladder without technical catalog jargon and ending on a seamless loop.
